previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with right leg cellulitis and fever after incomplete response to oral antibiotics. He was started on IV vancomycin, which was adjusted based on trough levels. Imaging ruled out DVT and fractures. His infection improved during the short hospital stay, and he was discharged home with a plan to complete a 10-day course of IV vancomycin during dialysis sessions. He was advised to continue all home medications, including those for gout, coronary artery disease, and hypertension, and to follow up with his primary care provider regarding medication adherence.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ YO M with ESRD on HD and coronary artery 
disease with known LAD 50% stenosis and ___ 2 to the RCA at 
catheterization ___ years ago who presented with similar anginal 
type pain - once at rest and the other following HD - along with 
elevated troponin (not above baseline) that has been stable and 
nonspecific EKG changes. ___ P-MIBI showed new reversible 
perfusion defect in the inferior wall likely representing 
restenosis of the RCA stent. He underwent catheterization ___ 
with ballooning of old RCA stent as well as placement of new DES 
to the RCA.

# CAD: Given the patient's risk factors and story, there was 
concern for unstable angina/NSTEMI. The patient had nonspecific 
EKG changes in the inferior leads which were thought to be 
consistent with restenosis of RCA stent. His troponin was 
elevated at admission but not above his baseline and did not 
progress (i.e., no acute rise and fall to suggest an acute 
event). New perfusion defects in the inferior wall on P-MIBI 
indicated potential restenosis of RCA so he underwent 
catheterization with ballooning of previous RCA stent and 
placement of new DES to RCA. MB did not rise post-cath. There 
was no evidence of hematoma or aneurysm at arteriotomy site. The 
patient was continued on aspirin 325 mg daily, clopidogrel 75 mg 
daily, simvastatin 80 mg daily, and Toprol XL 100 mg daily.

# Pump: Patient has no known CHF. Appearred euvolemic on 
admission exam with some increased volume prior to dialysis.

# Rhythm: NSR on EKG. No history of arrhythmias. Patient was 
monitored on tele without evidence of arrhythmia.

# ESRD (oliguric): on HD MWF. Completed HD ___ prior to 
admission. Has right sided graft for access. Renal followed the 
patient in-house for dialysis needs. Patient's K+ elevated to 
5.4 so he received Kayexelate in order to facilitate cardiac 
catheterization. He underwent angiography with dye load on 
___ and was dialyzed a few hours later as ___ is his 
normal dialysis day and dye can increase risk of pulmonary 
edema. The patient did not have any pain with dialysis and lungs 
remained clear.

# Hypertension: Stopped atenolol and changed to metoprolol as 
above. Added Lisinopril 10 mg daily as well.

# Hyperlipidemia: Continued simvastatin 80 mg.
